transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?
What finally made me say something is that after I eat too much, I go upstairs and make myself throw up. Then I act like I’m just tidying the kitchen or getting ready for bed.
When this happens, do you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

Yes. If no one’s in the kitchen, I can eat through leftovers from a church supper, crackers and cheese, cookies, whatever I made for book club—just all of it in one sitting. It’s much more than I’d ever put on a plate for myself at a normal meal.
When you eat that way, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?
Yes. Once I start, it’s like a switch flips. Part of me is saying, “Linda, stop,” but I just keep reaching for more food anyway.
Besides making yourself vomit, do you ever do anything else after eating to try to prevent weight gain?
Yes. The next day I’ll skip breakfast and lunch, or I’ll push myself to do extra laps with my walking group. It’s not because I have the energy for it—I’m trying to undo what I ate.
How much does your weight or body shape affect how you feel about yourself as a person?
I’m not sure how to separate it, honestly. I know I feel better about myself when I think I look thinner, and worse when I don’t. It affects my confidence quite a bit.
Are you currently at a very low body weight for your height?
I’m not really sure what counts as very low for my height. I don’t think of myself as particularly underweight, though.
About how often do these binge-and-purge episodes happen?
Since last winter, it’s been at least once most weeks—hardly a week goes by without one of those episodes and then me trying to make up for it.
What is your current height and weight?
I’m not sure of my exact weight right now—I haven’t checked recently. I’m about average height, I think, but I don’t know the precise measurement.
Has a doctor or anyone else told you that you are underweight?
My daughter and a woman from church have both said I look too thin. But I still panic if my skirt feels snug or if the scale goes up even a pound—it feels like I’ve become huge overnight.
Have you had a menstrual period in the last few months?
I’m not really sure—I haven’t been keeping track of that.
Have you lost a lot of weight recently?
I don’t know, really. I haven’t been weighing myself regularly enough to say.
Do your clothes fit much more loosely now than they used to?
I’m not sure, really. I haven’t noticed my clothes fitting much looser than they used to.
Has a doctor ever told you your weight was dangerously low for your height?
No, I don’t think a doctor has ever told me that.
For at least the past three months, have these binge-and-purge episodes been happening about once a week or more?
Yes. Since last winter, I don’t think there’s been many weeks without at least one time when I’ve eaten like that and then tried to make up for it—by being sick, skipping meals, or walking too much.
Would you say your current weight is significantly below what is considered healthy for your height?
I’m not really sure what would count as significantly below. I don’t think of myself as being especially underweight.
What clothing size do you wear right now?
I’m not sure, to be honest. I haven’t really paid attention to my clothing size lately.
What is your current weight in pounds?
I honestly don’t know my current weight. I haven’t weighed myself recently.
What is the lowest weight you remember being in the past year?
I’m not sure. I really haven’t kept track of my weight over the past year.
Compared with other women your height, do you think your body weight is much lower than normal?
My daughter and a woman at church have said I look too thin, but I don’t really see it that way. If my skirt feels tight or the scale goes up even a pound, I panic like I’ve gotten huge.
Do you think you are currently underweight for your height?
I don’t really think of myself as underweight. My daughter and someone from church say I look too thin, but if my skirt feels tight or I’m up even a pound, I panic and feel like I’ve gotten huge.
